## The defect

`tests/interfaces/facades/test_bridge_programmatic_e2e_heldout.py::test_check_access_returns_a_typed_six_step_result`
fails intermittently with `assert 'FAIL' == 'PASS'` — the bridge access-check oracle reports a
step as FAIL in a full-suite run, and passes when its tier is run alone.

**Observed twice, by two independent sessions, on different days and different suite sizes:**

* Session log `skeletal-soaplike-caracal` (`8359-9a62-055f-4811`): *"Local full suite (bare
  pytest, matching CI): 13683 passed, 1 failed — test_check_access_returns_a_typed_six_step_result
  in tests/interfaces/facades/test_bridge_programmatic_e2e_heldout.py (Jira bridge…)"*
* During bug `0e1d-c698-c38d-4c3e`: `pytest tests/unit tests/interfaces tests/integration -q` gave
  **14156 passed, 55 skipped, 1 xfailed, 1 failed**, that same test, same `'FAIL' == 'PASS'`
  assertion. Re-running `pytest tests/interfaces -q` alone: **1958 passed, 0 failed**, that test
  included.

Passes in isolation, fails in the larger run — the signature of cross-tier pollution (shared
state, env, or ordering) rather than a defect in the assertion itself. The test shells out toward
a Jira instance, so an environment/credential dependency that some other tier mutates is a
leading candidate, but that is a **hypothesis, not a finding** — nobody has root-caused it.

## Why this is a bug and not a retry

`AGENTS.md`: *"A flaky test is a BUG to root-cause, never a retry."* A test that fails
intermittently in the full suite is exactly the oracle CI depends on. Until it is diagnosed, every
future agent that hits it must decide whether it is real, and the honest answer today is "nobody
knows" — which is what makes it expensive.

It has been observed twice and recorded **only in session logs**, which are not work items and do
not surface in `ready` / `next-batch`. That is why it keeps being re-discovered instead of fixed.

## Why it was not fixed in scope

Found while proving bug `0e1d-c698-c38d-4c3e` (live-DC pass-health fail-open). It is unrelated:
the test imports nothing from `tests/_child_diag.py` or `tests/external/live_jira_dc/`, and it also
predates that change (`skeletal-soaplike-caracal` observed it earlier). It is also outside that
ticket's file lane.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The failure is reproduced DETERMINISTICALLY — the specific ordering, tier combination, or
      shared state that triggers it is identified, and it can be made to fail on demand.
- [x] The root cause is a named changeable artifact, not "flakiness" or "an environment issue".
- [x] A RED test or a seeded reproduction proves the mechanism before the fix.
- [x] The fix addresses the CLASS (the shared state / ordering dependency), not just this one
      test — if another test shares the seam, it is swept.
- [x] The full suite passes repeatedly (not once) after the fix.
